key_insight: Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA) uses a tree-structured indexer to make sparse attention asymptotically subquadratic, including routing costs.
engineering_relevance: ZHA offers a path to longer-context pretrained LLMs through lightweight adaptation rather than training from scratch.
method: Recursively compress cached keys into a hierarchy of summaries.
Route queries top-down to select a sparse subset of keys for attention.
Increase tree depth with sequence length to keep per-query routing and attention costs sublinear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports adaptation via KL distillation over a few billion tokens, preserved retrieval and reasoning performance, robustness with trees up to six levels, and modeled scaling advantages beyond one million tokens.
watch_item: Hundreds-of-millions-to-billions-token contexts remain a projected capability; practical gains depend on efficient routing, memory management, and hardware implementation.
paper_title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer
